The AI Act imposes specific obligations on GPAI model providers when their models are integrated into high-risk SPAI systems. These obligations include ensuring that the high-risk requirements are met, particularly concerning the quality of training data. The Act requires that the provider of the GPAI model must furnish sufficient information to enable downstream providers to comply with the obligations of the AI Act. This includes documentation of the model's training and testing processes, as well as details about the data used for training.

However, significant challenges arise for downstream providers when integrating GPAI models into high-risk systems. One major hurdle is the difficulty in verifying whether the training of the GPAI model meets the necessary compliance standards for high-risk use cases. Downstream providers often lack the means to assess the adequacy of the training data, which is crucial for ensuring that the AI system does not produce biased or discriminatory outputs. Additionally, the information provided by GPAI model providers may be minimal due to intellectual property concerns, further hampering the ability of downstream providers to ensure compliance with the AI Act's requirements. This situation creates a complex landscape where downstream providers must navigate stringent legal obligations while facing practical limitations in verifying compliance.
